selectionReason: The next fifteen, in source-row order, of the absent frozen rows at least one of whose KANJIDIC2 readings is used by an existing word article that declares the kanji (an automatic alignment of each word's kana against the kanji's readings), the rule announced on issue 60 after batch 136. No word article is added: 18 existing articles each gain one link to a new card. A card quizzes each reading that a declaring word article uses, unless the pinned JMdict marks the spelling as ateji or the reading as gikun; name-only readings are never quizzed; a reading type with no such reading gets an empty quizzed list. All fifteen pass, so none is set aside. No existing kanji card and no other line of a word article changes. 61 rows of the 106-row group, 11 rows whose declaring articles use none of their KANJIDIC2 readings, and 644 rows with no declaring article remain.

review.execution: All four runs started after the previous one ended, each with at most one tool call in flight and no overlapping starts; each confirmation was a fresh agent of the same model family, given the author's statement on its family's initial report and allowed to read the original packet and that report. Both families confirmed the same final commit 7e3c101b, which was written before either confirmation started. The initial-gpt audit flags one recursive shell command over packet directories; this is a false positive, matching ** used as Python exponentiation to sample Bezier curves of the stroke files. The confirm-gpt audit flags one path outside the packet and report; this is the parent review-packets folder, used only as a base variable to build paths into the packet, the confirmation packet and the initial-gpt report.

Under the batch rule, readings with no declaring word article are listed but not quizzed. Nine cards quiz only their on reading (葬 ソウ, 薦 セン, 虚 キョ, 融 ユウ, 衆 シュウ, 衝 ショウ, 裁 サイ, 視 シ, 覧 ラン) and six only their kun reading (蒔 ま.く, 蓄 たくわ.える, 街 まち, 裂 さ.く, 裸 はだか, 覆 おお.う).
Some readings on the cards rest on a single dictionary entry or a Kanjipedia-only entry and are labelled as source-only where they appear; the card text is the authority for which.
Some titles share an English word with existing titles in another sense and are not excluded from each other's quiz options, except where a Notes bullet on the card says otherwise.
Each mnemonic is a modern-shape memory aid, labelled on the card as not etymology; component and stroke statements follow the pinned KanjiVG revision.
The reading audits are the author's Python ports of the Kotlin builder; no Kotlin cross-check was run.
The scope audits do not attribute reads made through shell commands or Python, so they can list files as unread that the reports say were read.
Several judgments rest partly on live reads of Digital Daijisen, Kanjipedia and Jisho pages, not on pinned copies in the packet.
This exact published runtime and ZIP are verified, not the remaining N1 set.
